_about: Written once by the installer and NEVER overwritten by an upgrade, and
never removed by an uninstall. Edit it freely; it is yours.
Paths are deliberately absent. The host reads them from the registry key
WebRoot, ConfigDir, LogDir), which the installer keeps current across
upgrades. Hard-coding an install path here would survive an upgrade that
moved it, and a supervisor pointing at a python.exe that is no longer
there is a service that does not start.
Restart the service after editing:  Restart-Service ChaosHost

Lan._comment: The gateway's LAN listener. The installer's firewall rule opens exactly this port, inbound, private profile only. Changing it here means the firewall rule no longer matches -- see docs/windows-deployment.md before you do.

Backend._comment: The supervised Python child. Loopback only, always: it is an unauthenticated control API and it is reached through the gateway, never directly from the LAN.
Backend._restart_comment: How hard to try when the backend dies. A homestead does not have someone watching the console; the supervisor keeps restarting, and the alarm for 'the backend is crash-looping' is the operator's signal, not a give-up counter.

Logging._comment: Files land in %ProgramData%\Project CHAOS\logs. Service lifecycle events also go to the Windows Application event log under the source 'ChaosHost' -- that is where to look when the service will not start at all.
